extracted.intended_audience: scientists, physicians, anthropometrists, and families interested in systematic anthropometric and medico-metric records
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for recording and testing the bodily measurements, photographs, physiological faculties, and medical life-history of individuals, and for organizing anthropometric/medico-metric laboratories and apparatus. Covers which measurements to take, basic test procedures, precautions, and record-keeping recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The features should be taken in full face and in exact profile, and on not too small a scale — that of about one seventh of the natural size being, perhaps, the most convenient. Also take other photographs in less formal attitudes to show the whole figure and gesture; in some of these the limbs might be more or less bared to exhibit the muscular development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full-face and exact profile views at ~1/7 natural size as standard. Supplement with less formal whole-figure photos to document posture, gesture, and muscle; include semi-bared limb photos where appropriate to show muscular development. Preserve these with family records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core anthropometric measurements (Anthropometric Committee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the rules of the Anthropometric Committee: measurements refer to height, to weight, to chest-girth (but only if taken by skilled observers on a uniform plan), to capacity of lungs (also under those conditions), and to color of hair and eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt standard protocols from recognized committees. Only record chest-girth and lung capacity when skilled observers use a uniform plan to avoid inconsistent data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential personal and parental data
rubrics_metrics.description: Record birthplace and residence, whether in town or country, both of the person and of his parents; also their race, whether English, Scotch, or Irish, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect simple demographic/contextual data alongside measurements to enable proper interpretation and grouping in later analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic remeasurement
rubrics_metrics.description: The tests would define the capacities of the person at the moment when he was observed. They are expected to be renewed at intervals, so as to serve as records of successive periods in his life-history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule repeated measurements at intervals to build longitudinal life-history records rather than single snapshots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and testing of energy and endurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy may be defined as the length of time during which a person is wont to work at full stretch, day by day, without harm to himself..., and endurance may be tested by records of such feats of sustained bodily or mental work as he may have recently performed, that were not succeeded next day by feverish excitement or by fatigue, but whose effects were entirely dissipated by a single night's rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer longitudinal records of sustained activities whose after-effects (or lack of them) can be observed; ideal physiological tests would measure waste over repair, but until these are standardized, use safe observable records and note context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength measurement by spring dynamometer
rubrics_metrics.description: The strength is best measured by a spring dynamometer, of which the frame-work is held in the left hand with the arm extended, while the spring is drawn back by the right hand in the attitude of an archer. It only refers to the strength of the arms, but that is in most cases sufficient to express the general muscular power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a spring dynamometer set-up as specified; record the posture and handedness. This test avoids injurious straining and serves as a practical proxy for general muscular power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dangerous maximal lifting tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials of lifting heavy weights are positively dangerous. If a multitude of persons were tested in that way, some instances of broken blood-vessels and of abdominal ruptures would be almost sure to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use maximal heavy-lift tests in mass anthropometric surveys; prefer safer dynamometer tests to prevent injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agility measurement standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agility may be defined in terms, say, of the number of seconds required to run a hundred yards, of the greatest horizontal distance that can be covered by a leap, of the distance to which a cricket-ball can be thrown, and by means of various gymnastic feats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select measurable, preferably indoor/confined-space gymnastic feats as standards; record times/distances (100-yard run, long jump, throwing distance) as comparable agility indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eye–hand coordination testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The co-ordination of muscles and eye is another faculty that varies widely...it seems a most simple faculty to be tested, nevertheless I know of no recognized methods of doing so; in default of one, the best plan of defining its amount might be, in the case of youths, by their measured skill in well-known games, as racquets, cricket, rifle-shooting, billiards...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When formal tests are absent, use standardized performance in target or precision games as proxy measures; always note prior training/practice since education increases this faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense-discrimination battery (sight, sound, touch, muscular)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify important simple tests: Sight — its keenness; the appreciation of different shades; that of different colors. Sound — its keenness; the appreciation of different grades of loudness; that of different notes. Touch — discrimination of different roughnesses, such as wire-work of differently sized mesh. Muscular Sense — discrimination of weights externally alike, but differing slightly in specific gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a simple inexpensive battery of discrimination tests drawn from psychophysics (brightness, color, loudness, pitch, texture, weight differences) suitable for routine anthropometric labs; choose instruments that are effective yet quick to manipulate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction time (rate of response) testing
rubrics_metrics.description: A signal is given to one of the senses...to which response is made by pressing a stop. The interval between the signal and the response is measurable, and it differs in different persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple stimulus–response apparatus (visual, auditory, tactile) and measure signal-to-response interval; standardize the signal and response method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple judgment (choice reaction) time test
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrangement is made for two possible and different signals, which are severally to be responded to by different forms of response...After he perceives it, there is an appreciable time of hesitation before he is able to make the appropriate response, and this time is easily measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include binary-choice tasks to measure decision/judgment time in addition to simple reaction time; quantify the extra hesitation produced by choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence of impressions / after-image testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The persistence of impressions, especially if visual ones, is exceeding various...after gazing at a red wafer ... the appearance of a green after-image will be present to some and not to others. There can be little doubt that the liability to after-images is an important factor of the artistic temperament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate standardized after-image/contrast tests (e.g., color wafer exposures) to assess susceptibility; note potential links to temperament and artistic tendency; systematize such tests for anthropometric use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory testing (multi-sensory dependence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The memory, in its dependence on the relative impressions of eye, ear, and other senses, whether severally or in combination, admits of being tested...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consolidated, reproducible experiments to assess memory across sensory modalities; record modalities used and testing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record previous practice when reporting tests
rubrics_metrics.description: When recording the results of any test it would be sufficient to append a brief note concerning the amount of previous practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always document the subject's prior practice/training level because practice rapidly increases performance initially and affects comparability of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select inexpensive, quick instruments for routine labs
rubrics_metrics.description: Out of all the contrivances that have been devised for these experiments...we want a battery of the most simple ones that are sufficiently effective for ordinary anthropometric purposes...to select out of extant instruments those that are sufficiently inexpensive and quick in manipulation to be appropriately placed in an anthropometric laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize instruments that balance sensitivity with cost and speed to enable widespread adoption in routine anthropometric laboratories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for laboratory use and intelligent operators
rubrics_metrics.description: They cannot be properly utilized for ordinary anthropometric purposes without such apparatus as would require to be kept in a laboratory and used under the guidance of an intelligent operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that many delicate tests require a lab setting and trained personnel; ensure qualified operators run and interpret measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish anthropometric and medico-metric laboratories
rubrics_metrics.description: When shall we have anthropometric laboratories, where a man may from time to time get himself and his children weighed, measured, and rightly photographed, and have each of their bodily faculties tested, by the best methods known to modern science?...There seems to be need for medico-metric laboratories where certificates of observed facts should be furnished to any applicant for stated fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote creation of public or institutional labs that provide standardized measurement and certification services; these labs would serve physicians and the public and act as repositories for repeated measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical life-history record-keeping by physicians
rubrics_metrics.description: The data for the medical history of a man's life are the observations made by his physician in his successive illnesses, and I would dwell on the importance of gradually establishing a custom that the medical attendant of each patient should as a matter of course write down such clinical notes of his case as are written at the bedsides of public patients at hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage physicians to produce bedside-style clinical notes and preserve prescriptions for patients; these should be kept by the patient to form an accumulative medical life-history useful to future care and hereditary inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motives and uses for systematic measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: The motives that might induce a person to take the trouble of getting himself accurately measured and appraised ...: 1. Their biographical interest to the person himself, to his family, and descendants. 2. Their utility, especially from a medical point of view, to himself in after-life. 3. The information they might give of hereditary dangers and vital probabilities to his descendants. 4. Their value as future materials for much‑needed investigations into the statistics of life-histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When advocating measurement programs, emphasize these concrete benefits to encourage participation and the creation of family registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematize instruments and agree on a standard outfit
rubrics_metrics.description: It would require much practice and consideration by capable men before a standard outfit could be decided on. A few shelves would hold the necessary apparatus. Something useful of the kind could be set on foot at a moment's notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work toward consensus on a standard, practical set of apparatus for anthropometric/medico-metric labs; start with a compact, shelf‑portable kit and refine it through practice.
